text.p: Alberta Energy Co Ltd, which last year completed at C$1.1 billion friendly merger with Conwest Exploration Co, is approaching potential new deals gingerly but is not ruling out the prospect, AEC chief executive Gwyn Morgan said on Thursday.

"There would be assets we'd like to have, but the market is pretty overheated -- the values in most cases are beyond what suit us," Morgan told Reuters following a presentation to an energy industry audience.

AEC, now one of the world's top 10 public exploration and production firms in terms of size, has recently been touted as a potential suitor in numerous deals, in the works or speculated on, in the takeover-happy Canadian oil patch.

"With the combination of AEC and Conwest, we've got a tremendous amount of land and a tremendous amount of opportunities, so we're not in a situation where growing the company means an acquisition," he said.

Last year's merger with Conwest, which was praised by analysts for the speed at which the firms melded together, saw AEC's market capitalization grow to C$3.5 billion from C$1.6 billion at the end of 1995.

The company, now split up into three semi-autonomous upstream operating regions in western Canada, expects to produce 600 million cubic feet per day of natural gas and 65,000 barrels of oil in 1997 while drilling about 450 wells.
It also has extensive "midstream" assets, such as the huge AECO-C gas storage hub in Alberta, and a pipeline division, 30 percent of which is about to be offered to the public.

"I wouldn't want to rule out ever making another acquisition, it's just that it would have to be at the right place at the right time and add value," Morgan said, adding that he favored friendly deals over hostile ones.
Unlike several companies being touted as takeover candidates, Conwest was a successful exploration firm not in the market for a merger when approached by AEC in 1995.
Today, the AEC's size and scope place it near many other firms' operations, fueling deal speculation.

AEC was touted in industry circles last week as a possible white knight for Wascana Energy Inc, target of a C$1.7 billion bid from Talisman Energy Inc. Wascana chief executive Frank Proto was president of AEC's pipeline division before assuming his current post.

AEC is in the process of bolstering its heavy oil operations in eastern Alberta, including launching a high-tech pilot project aimed at recovering an estimated 21 billion barrels of heavy oil in place at Primrose.
Wascana is known largely for its large heavy oil production across the provincial border in Saskatchewan.
Another firm recently mentioned as a potential takeover target is Elan Energy Inc. It, too, has heavy oil production along the Alberta-Saskatchewan border.

AEC has also been speculated as a suitor for Chauvco Resources Ltd, whose two major shareholders, Gendis Inc and Trimac Ltd, have recently undergone major restructurings, throwing shareholding into question.

Chauvco operates production in Argentina and the northwest Alberta/northeast British Columbia region. AEC is growing its exploration presense in Argentina and is a major force along the Canadian Rocky Mountain foothills.
"We always have a list of ideal assets," Morgan said. "But there's a big difference between having a list and figuring you can get good value."
